problem:
A website is tracking the rate at which new users sign up. The rate $r(t)$ at which users sign up is given by the function

$$
r(t)=12\cdot {2}^{t/3},
$$

where $r(t)$ is measured in users per day, and $t>0$ is the time in days.

Between $t=3$ and $t=9$ days, to nearest integer,
{{field-1}} users signed up.
worked_solution:
We are given the signup rate $r(t)$ in users per day. To find the number of users that signed up between the times $t=3$ and $t=9$ days, we integrate $r(t)$ between these two limits. This gives:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{3}^{9}12\cdot {2}^{t/3}\,\text{d}t & ={12\cdot \frac{3\cdot {2}^{t/3}}{\operatorname{ln}⁡2}|}_{3}^{9} \\  & ={36\cdot \frac{{2}^{t/3}}{\operatorname{ln}⁡2}|}_{3}^{9} \\  & =\frac{36}{\operatorname{ln}⁡2}({2}^{3}-{2}^{1}) \\  & =\frac{216}{\operatorname{ln}⁡2} \\  & ≈312\end{aligned}
$$

rounded to the nearest integer. 

Therefore, between $t=3$ and $t=9$ days, $312$ users signed up.
